verdict.rationale: Orb documents day-based proration on plan changes: it credits the unused portion of the period. It keeps a complete audit trail of every plan assignment and lets you preview invoice impact before saving subscription edits such as seat quantity changes with scheduled effective dates. The evidence does not show how prorated credits and partial-period charges appear as invoice line items, nor any rounding or penny-level reconciliation rules. Missing for 10: documented invoice line-item breakdown of prorated credits/charges, rounding and penny-level reconciliation rules, explicit upgrade vs downgrade proration behavior, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, mid-cycle upgrades and downgrades are prorated with documented, auditable math — credits, partial periods, and invoice line items that reconcile to the penny

citations.quote: Orb will credit the customer an amount corresponding to the portion of the time period that was left unused using day-based proration.
Orb maintains a complete audit trail of every plan assignment.
Preview the billing and invoice impact before you save, so you can confirm how charges and invoices will look.
update fixed-fee quantities (seats), apply or edit discounts, maximums, minimums, and schedule effective dates
